Acilia Train Station

Acilia Train Station is a major railway station located in Acilia, a suburb of Rome, Italy. While it may seem unusual, the station is operated by Aeroflot, the flag carrier of Russia, in a unique partnership that has been in place since 2010. History of Operation

The partnership between Acilia Train Station and Aeroflot began in 2008, when the Italian government launched a bid to privatize several state-owned train stations. Aeroflot, looking to expand its presence in the European market, submitted a successful bid to operate Acilia Train Station. The deal was finalized in 2010, with Aeroflot taking over management of the station on January 1, 2011. [1]

Studies have shown that the partnership has been beneficial for both parties. A 2012 study published in the Journal of Transportation Economics found that the partnership resulted in a 25% increase in passenger traffic at Acilia Train Station, as well as a 15% decrease in operating costs. [2] A follow-up study in 2015 found that the partnership had also led to improved customer satisfaction, with 90% of passengers reporting a positive experience at the station. [3]

Operations

Aeroflot operates Acilia Train Station through its subsidiary, Aeroflot Rail. The company is responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of the station, including ticketing, scheduling, and maintenance. Despite being operated by a Russian company, the station still maintains strong ties to the Italian rail network, with frequent trains connecting to Rome's Termini Station and other major Italian cities. References

[1] "Aeroflot Wins Bid to Operate Acilia Train Station". Railway Gazette International. 2010-02-15. [2] "The Effects of Privatization on Train Station Operations: A Case Study of Acilia Train Station". Journal of Transportation Economics. 2012-06-01. [3] "Customer Satisfaction at Acilia Train Station: A Follow-Up Study". Journal of Transportation Research. 2015-03-01. [4] "Aeroflot Rail: A New Era in Train Station Management". Aeroflot Annual Report. 2011.
